specific_competences.main_competence: Demonstrate mastery of the structure of the Earth
specific_competences.specific_competence: Demonstrate an understanding of the origin and the structure of the Earth and Earth systems
learning_activities: (a) Explain the concept and scope of Geography (branches, importance and relationship with other disciplines)
(b) Describe the Earth (origin, shape, size, position and movements of the earth in the solar system, and parallels and meridians)
teaching_methods: Brainstorming: In manageable groups students brainstorm on the meaning, branches and importance of Geography, and relationship between Geography and other disciplines Field Observation: Guide students to observe landforms, vegetations and human activities to support the concept of geography and summarise their importance in relationship to other disciplines

Brainstorming: Guide students to brainstorm and present about the origin, shape, size, position and movements of the earth in the solar system, and parallels and meridians Field Observation: Guide students to observe the Earth’s surface and identify some of the components of the solar system Project work: Group students to design a model on the components of the solar system (size, shape, distance, position), and then present in class
assessment_criteria: Basic concepts of Geography are clearly explained
resources: Relevant books, charts, and ICT simulation tools on the concept of Geography
Relevant books, globe, picture of solar system, relevant ICT simulation tools and models on the planet earth

specific_competences.main_competence: Demonstrate mastery of the structure of the Earth
specific_competences.specific_competence: Demonstrate an understanding of the major features of the Earth surface
learning_activities: (a) Describe major features of the Earth’s surface (continents, oceans, major relief features, large inland water bodies and vegetation zones)
teaching_methods: Questions &Answers: Guide students to mention landforms available in their surroundings Field observation: Guide students to visit the nearby landforms, vegetation and water bodies available in their communities to examine the formation, distribution and their importance to the communities Group Discussion: Guide students to discuss the size and distribution of continents, then present in the class
assessment_criteria: The major features of the Earth are correctly described
resources: Environment, relevant books, relief maps, globe/models, and relevant ICT simulation tools

specific_competences.main_competence: Demonstrate mastery of the structure of the Earth
specific_competences.specific_competence: Demonstrate an understanding of the origin and the structure of the Earth and earth systems
learning_activities: (a) Describe the internal structure of the Earth (crust, mantle, core) and their major characteristics (location, size/ thickness, density and gross composition)
(b) Describe the main external Earth systems (Hydrosphere, Atmosphere and Biosphere)
teaching_methods: Brainstorming: Guide students to brainstorm on the internal structure of the Earth Group work: Assign students to design models and drawings to characterise the internal structure of the Earth

Questions &Answers: Guide students to explain the main external earth systems Field observation: Guide students to observe and discuss the hydrosphere, atmosphere and biosphere with cases from their communities Independent library study: Organise students to to examine the main external earth systems
assessment_criteria: The internal structure of the Earth is correctly described
The external structure of the Earth is correctly described
resources: Relevant books, globe/models, environment, and flash with content on internal structure of the earth
Relevant books, globe/models, environment, and relevant ICT tools, flash with content on external structure of the earth (atmosphere, hydrosphere, biosphere and cryosphere)

specific_competences.main_competence: Demonstrate mastery of basic skills and techniques in Geography
specific_competences.specific_competence: Demonstrate an understanding of the basic techniques of map and photograph interpretation
learning_activities: (a) Describe the basic principles of reading and interpreting maps (key, symbols, direction, margin/frame, map title, scale and contour patterns) (b) Reading and interpreting various type of maps and their importance (topographical and statistical map)
(b) Describe the basic concept of photograph in Geography (meaning, types, elements and uses)
(c) Describe the basic principles of photograph interpretation (identifying foreground, middle ground and background, associating objects with geographical phenomena)
teaching_methods: Brainstorming: Guide students to brainstorm the basic principles of reading and interpreting maps Group Discussion Guide students to discuss basic principles of reading and interpreting maps Case Study Guide students to interpret and analyse various types of maps and their importance to the community

Brainstorming: Guide students to brainstorm the meaning, types, elements and importance of photographs in Geography Group Discussion Guide students to discuss the basic uses of photographs in Geography Guest Speaker Invite resourceful persons (e.g., cartographer, photographer, camera man/woman) to share their experiences on uses of photographs

Question & Answers: Guide students to discuss basic principles of photograph interpretation Group Discussion Guide students to identify different parts of photographs, interpret them and make association with geographical phenomena Case Study Guide students to use photographs to interpret different cases of geographical phenomena
assessment_criteria: The basic principles of reading and interpretation of maps are clearly explained
The concept of photograph and its contents are clearly explained
The basic principles of interpretation of photography are clearly described
resources: Maps, relevant books, and relevant ICT simulation tools
Relevant books and photographs (ground, vertical and oblique), magazine/ newspapers, camera, and relevant ICT tools)
Relevant books on photographs, photographs (ground, vertical and oblique), magazine/ newspapers, and relevant ICT tools

specific_competences.main_competence: Demonstrate mastery of the structure of the Earth
specific_competences.specific_competence: Demonstrate an understanding of the relationship between relief, climate and natural vegetation
learning_activities: (a) Describe the major climatic regions of the world (tropical, temperate, polar and sub-tropical)
(b) Describe the relationship between major features of the Earth’s surface, climate, and natural vegetation
teaching_methods: Brainstorming: Guide students to brainstorm on major world climatic regions Group Discussion: Guide students to characterise the major world climatic regions Field visit: Guide students to observe local climate characteristics and associate them with the world climatic regions Graphical and Maps presentation: Guide students to draw graphs and maps to characterise major world climatic regions

Question & Answers: Guide students to describe the relationship between major features of the Earth’s surface, climate and natural vegetation Case study: Guide students to justify the relationship between major features of the Earth’s surface, climate and natural vegetation
assessment_criteria: The major climatic regions of the World are categorised or classified clearly
The relationship between major features of the Earth’s surface, climate and natural vegetation are correctly described
resources: Map, graphs, photographs, globe, variety of living organisms, and online materials on the major climatic regions of the world.
Maps, photographs, globe and online materials on the relationship between major features of the earth’s surface, climate and natural vegetations

specific_competences.main_competence: Demonstrate mastery of basic skills and techniques in Geography
specific_competences.specific_competence: Demonstrate an understanding of the basic techniques in land surveying
learning_activities: (a) Explore the basic tenets of surveying (meaning, types, equipment, methods, and importance)
teaching_methods: Group Discussion: Guide students to explain the basic concepts of surveying Brainstorming: Guide students to brainstorm on methods and importance of surveying Guest speaker: Invite resourceful persons from surveying institutions/ companies to share experiences on surveying activities

Project work: Guide students to carry out simple surveying activities around the schools and their local communities Guest speaker: Invite resourceful persons from surveying institutions/ companies to share experiences and conduct simple surveying activities Group Discussion Guide students to discuss and apply the findings from surveying on socio-economic and environmental activities
assessment_criteria: The basic tenets of surveying are correctly explored
The simple tape/ chain surveying is correctly carried out
resources: Relevant books on land surveying, tape measure/chain, Arrows, plumb bob, cross-staff ranging poles, pegs, notebook, pencil/pen, and relevant ICT tools
Relevant books on land surveying, tape measure/chain, Arrows, plumb bob, cross-staff ranging poles, pegs, notebook, pencil/pen, and relevant ICT tools

specific_competences.specific_competence: Carry out a project in Geography
learning_activities: (a) Develop and carry out a simple research project in Geography
teaching_methods: Project work: Guide students in groups to prepare a good research title for the project Field work: Guide students to conduct a simple research project in the field on geographical research titles of their choice.
assessment_criteria: The research title of each group is correctly prepared A simple research project is effectively conducted in the field by each group
resources: Environment, institutions, note books, pen, pencil, key informants, camera/smart- phones, and relevant ICT tools

specific_competences.specific_competence: Demonstrate an understanding of the relationship between geography, environmental health, human settlements and economic activities
learning_activities: (a) Describe the geographical factors that influence the spatial distribution of population, human settlements and economic activities (climate, soil, relief, vegetation, transport and water supply)
(b) Examine the impacts of population distribution on economic activities and the environment (land use and settlement patterns changes)
teaching_methods: Field observation: Guide students to observe and discuss on the types and characteristics of human settlements and settlement patterns from the surrounding communities Brainstorming: Guide students to brainstorm the factors influencing population distribution and human settlements Case studies: Guide students to apply different cases of human settlements and link them with geographical factors

Brainstorming: Guide students to brainstorm about the impacts of population distribution on economic activities and the environment Group Discussion: Guide students to discuss and present in class on the impacts of population distribution on sustainability of the environment Field observation: Guide students to observe and summarise the relationship between population distribution and environmental change (land use change, change in settlement patterns etc) Case studies: Guide students to apply different cases from local communities to show the relationship between population distribution and the environment
assessment_criteria: The geographical factors that influence the spatial distribution of population, human settlements and economic activities are clearly described
The impacts of population distribution on economic activities and the environment are clearly explained
resources: Relevant books on human settlement, population distribution, National census reports, data from birth and death rate, and migration
Relevant books on human settlement, population, photographs on human settlement patterns environment

specific_competences.specific_competence: Carry out a project in Geography
learning_activities: (a) Complete and submit a report of the project started in Form Three
teaching_methods: Project work: Guide students to write a report for the project started in Form Three Role Play Organise students to practice report presentations on geographical research Group Presentation: Organise students to present and submit a report for assessment
assessment_criteria: The assessment of the project started in Form Three is completed and submitted on time
resources: Relevant books on geographical research, research reports, and relevant ICT tools
